before:
Peninsular Lamp Room Museum — Accession Catalogue, Working Order

The volunteer cataloguing team meets on alternate Tuesdays through the winter closure. Material arriving from the decommissioned north light is entered in the ledger as it is unpacked, but the order in which it is written up is fixed by the team's standing arrangement: items carrying a named donor are written up ahead of items carrying only a dated provenance, and dated provenance ahead of unattributed finds from the store shed. Nothing is excluded on these grounds; the whole backlog is entered before the season ends, and any volunteer may work on any tray. The arrangement only settles what is handled first when two trays are open at once and the afternoon is short.

before:
Saltmarsh Causeway — Seasonal Notice to Foot Traffic

The causeway to the Old Quarantine Jetty stands about one metre above chart datum at its lowest span and is under water for roughly four hours either side of high water. Between the first of October and the last day of March, walkers may use the causeway during the marked safe window provided a second person waits at the landward gate. The tide boards at each end are read at dawn by the harbour watchkeeper and repainted each spring. Persons crossing outside the marked window do so beyond the assistance of the watchkeeper, whose station closes at dusk throughout the winter months.
after:
Saltmarsh Causeway — Seasonal Notice to Foot Traffic

Between the first of October and the last day of March, walkers are forbidden to use the causeway at any state of tide unless accompanied by the watchkeeper. variation_site: The sentence covering winter foot traffic across the causeway differs between the two versions.
author_note: Changes what is permitted while leaving every tidal and station description untouched; the surrounding measurements tempt an empirical reading.

before:
Fenland Bellringers' Guild — Tower Handbook, Section 4

Dear fellow ringer, we do hope you will forgive a small word about the ringing chamber floor. It has been swept before you arrived and we would be ever so grateful if boots left muddy from the drove roads could be changed at the porch step rather than at the rope circle. The vestry keeps a basket of spare shoes for anyone caught out. Tea money goes in the tin on the sill, and the last person down puts the guard across the stair. None of this is new; it is simply set down here so that visiting bands know what the local practice has always been on a wet practice night.

before:
Upland Bothy Association — Water Supply Policy, Northern Group

Each bothy in the northern group draws from a surface burn above the building. The association's position on treatment is set out here for wardens and for visiting parties. On the evidence of the two sampling rounds carried out during the summer, the burn above Coirebeg carries livestock contamination for several weeks after the hill is stocked, and parties should boil water taken there. Wardens are asked to note the stocking dates in the bothy book so that later parties can judge for themselves. Filters supplied by the association are held at the trustees' store and issued on request to anyone undertaking a long stay through the winter season.

before:
Borough Allotments Committee — Report on Bonfire Complaints

Twenty-two complaints were received between February and April, chiefly from the terraces backing onto the Sandgate site. Burning on borough allotment land is governed by byelaw 14, made in 1976 under the general powers, which forbids burning before four in the afternoon. Officers checked the seventeen complaints that gave a time and found that eleven of them named a morning hour. No enforcement was undertaken this season. The committee is asked to note the pattern and to consider whether a reminder card at the gates would serve better than correspondence, which in past seasons has not reduced the volume of complaints arriving at the office.

before:
Coastal Herbarium — Mounting Bench Working Sequence

Sheets arriving from the drying press are handled at the mounting bench by one worker at a time. Take the specimen from the press folder, rinse the sand from the fronds in the shallow tray, and then weigh the sample on the bench balance before it is laid on the card. Strapping is applied at four points, the label is gummed at the lower right, and the sheet goes to the rack for two days. The obligations of the mounter are as set out in the volunteer agreement: gloves at all times, no eating at the bench, and every sheet initialled. Damaged fronds are reported to the curator rather than discarded.

before:
Tidal Mill Trust — Registry of Mooring Charges, Winter Quarter

The registry lists each holder, the berth reference, and the sum falling due on the quarter day. Charges entered in this quarter are worked out from the banded scale of 2019, applying the band that matches each berth. Arrears carry the usual eight weeks' grace before the berth is offered on. Two berths remain vacant at the mill wall following the silting survey, and no sum is entered against them. Holders disputing an entry write to the harbour clerk within twenty-one days, enclosing the previous quarter's demand. The registry is copied to the trustees before each meeting and kept in the strong cupboard in the counting house.
after:
Tidal Mill Trust — Registry of Mooring Charges, Winter Quarter

The registry lists each holder, the berth reference, and the sum falling due on the quarter day. Charges entered in this quarter are worked out from the flat per-metre tariff, applying the rate to the measured length of each berth. Arrears carry the usual eight weeks' grace before the berth is offered on. Two berths remain vacant at the mill wall following the silting survey, and no sum is entered against them. Holders disputing an entry write to the harbour clerk within twenty-one days, enclosing the previous quarter's demand. The registry is copied to the trustees before each meeting and kept in the strong cupboard in the counting house.

before:
Market Hall Caretakers' Manual — Definitions and Timings

Throughout this manual, a working day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays. Every interval given below is counted in working days on that footing. Repairs reported at the lodge are acknowledged within one working day and made good within five. Stallholders give three working days' notice of a change of pitch. Refunds on cancelled lettings are paid within ten. The caretaker's own leave is counted in the same units when cover is arranged with the hall committee. Where an interval falls partly in the closed fortnight after Christmas, the counting resumes on the first day the hall reopens to traders in the new year.
after:
Market Hall Caretakers' Manual — Definitions and Timings

Throughout this manual, a working day means Monday to Saturday, including public holidays other than Christmas Day. Every interval given below is counted in working days on that footing. Repairs reported at the lodge are acknowledged within one working day and made good within five. Stallholders give three working days' notice of a change of pitch. Refunds on cancelled lettings are paid within ten. The caretaker's own leave is counted in the same units when cover is arranged with the hall committee. Where an interval falls partly in the closed fortnight after Christmas, the counting resumes on the first day the hall reopens to traders in the new year.
variation_site: The opening sentence fixing the units used throughout the manual differs between the two versions.
author_note: Redefines a term that every later interval composes over, so all the stated timings shift with it; reads at first like a mere factual detail.

before:
Tern Island Wardens — Bulletin, Late June

The colony count was completed on the twenty-third in fair weather with two counters working from the eastern hide. Forty-one occupied nests were recorded on the shingle spit, with a further nine on the raft. Predation signs were confined to the northern end. The electric fence held through the spring tides and needed one repair after the gale. Visitors are reminded that the spit remains closed until the second week of August and that the hide window is not to be opened while counts are in progress. Ringing sessions resume once the last clutches have hatched, and volunteers should contact the warden's hut for dates.
